reasons: Both answers give nearly the same plan: check the pipeline, normalize complaints against past windows and look for reporting bias, compare per-class results, label fresh tickets for both models, and apply a cost-weighted decision rule with shadow mode. A adds a check on whether complaints are valid, explicit reweighting by the production class mix, and a clear decision table. B adds error distance, overfitting of the prompt to the test set, changes in how complaints are logged, and replaying the complained-about tickets through the old model, so neither answer comes out clearly ahead.

A: Claims that 90% inter-annotator agreement puts the 87 vs 91% difference in the noise zone, which conflates label noise with a comparison between models on the same labels (overstated)
